title: Audio Not Working
cardText: Troubleshoot missing, low or distorted sound on a Windows computer.
Check volume, output devices, speakers, headphones, Bluetooth connections and audio settings.
Diagnose audio services, drivers and possible hardware faults.
text: This guide helps diagnose sound problems on a Windows computer.
Start with volume and mute settings before changing drivers or services.
Check that sound is being sent to the correct speakers, headset or monitor.
Test different applications and audio devices to isolate the fault.
The menu names shown are primarily for Windows 11 and may differ in Windows 10.

checkMute.title: Check whether audio is muted
body: Select the speaker icon on the Windows taskbar.
Check that the speaker is not muted.
Check any keyboard mute key or function key.
If using external speakers or headphones, check their physical mute and volume controls.

unmuteAudio.title: Unmute the audio
body: Unmute Windows and any connected speaker or headset.
Play a known working audio file or video.
If sound is still missing, restart this guide and continue with the volume checks.

checkVolumeLevel.title: Check Windows and application volume
body: Open Settings, System, Sound, then Volume mixer.
Check the main system volume.
Under Apps, confirm the affected application is not muted and its volume is turned up.
Check the application's own volume control if it has one.
Check that the app is using the intended output device.

link.name: Microsoft: Fix low or quiet sound
link.description: Official instructions for checking Windows volume, Volume mixer and sound settings.

checkVolumeLevel.alt: Windows 11 Volume mixer showing system and individual application volume controls
checkVolumeLevel.caption: Check both the system volume and the affected application's volume.

increaseVolume.title: Adjust the volume
body: Increase the system and application volume to a comfortable level.
Unmute any application that was muted.
Check the speaker or headset volume controls as well.
Test sound again. If the issue remains, continue with the other checks.

testAudioPlayback.title: Test sound in different applications
body: Play a known working audio file or video.
Try another application or a different source of sound.
If sound works in one application but not another, the problem may be application-specific.
If there is no sound from any application, continue checking Windows audio output.

appSpecificIssue.title: Application-specific audio problem
body: Sound works in some applications but not others.
Open Windows Volume mixer and check the affected application's volume and output device.
Check the application's own audio settings.
Close and reopen the affected application, then test again.
If needed, update or repair the application.

link.name: Microsoft: Fix application audio
link.description: Official instructions for cases where system audio works but individual applications have no sound.

checkOutputDevice.title: Check the selected audio output device
body: Open Windows Settings, System, Sound.
Under Output, check which device is selected.
Choose the speakers, headphones or headset you actually want to use.
Windows may send sound to a connected monitor over HDMI or DisplayPort, a USB headset or a Bluetooth device.
Check that the selected device is enabled.
Use the Test option where available.

link.name: Microsoft: Fix sound and audio problems
link.description: Official steps for choosing the correct default audio output device.

checkOutputDevice.alt: Windows 11 Sound settings showing available speakers and headset output devices
checkOutputDevice.caption: Select the output device you actually want to hear sound through.

selectCorrectDevice.title: Select the correct audio device
body: Select the correct speakers or headphones in Windows Sound settings.
If necessary, set the device as the default output.
Play audio to confirm it is working.
If there is still no sound, continue checking the connected audio hardware.

checkHeadphonesSpeakers.title: Check speakers and headphones
body: If using external speakers, check that they are powered on and their volume is turned up.
Confirm the audio cable is connected to the correct port.
For a desktop computer, check that the speakers are not plugged into a microphone or line-in socket.
Reconnect the headset or speakers and check for damaged cables.
If possible, test the speakers or headphones on another device.

repairAudioDevice.title: Repair or replace the audio device
body: The speakers, headphones or their connection appear faulty.
Check the cable, power supply and audio connector as applicable.
Try a known-working replacement device.
If sound returns with another device, repair or replace the faulty equipment.

checkBluetoothAudio.title: Check Bluetooth audio
body: Open Windows Settings, Bluetooth & devices.
Check whether a Bluetooth headset or speaker is connected.
Confirm Windows is not sending audio to a Bluetooth device that is switched off or in another room.
If using Bluetooth audio, confirm the device is connected and selected as the output.
Temporarily disconnect unnecessary Bluetooth audio devices and test again.

link.name: Microsoft: Bluetooth connected but no sound
link.description: Official troubleshooting for Bluetooth speakers and headsets connected without working audio.

disconnectBluetooth.title: Correct the Bluetooth audio connection
body: Disconnect any Bluetooth audio device that should not be receiving sound.
If using Bluetooth headphones or speakers, reconnect them and select them as the Windows output.
Check the Bluetooth device's battery level.
Test sound again. If the problem remains, continue with Windows audio checks.

checkAudioEnhancements.title: Check audio enhancements
body: Open Windows Settings, System, Sound and select the affected output device.
Find Audio enhancements and temporarily turn them off if available.
Also disable spatial sound temporarily when troubleshooting distorted or missing audio.
Play a test sound again.
If audio improves, leave the problematic enhancement disabled.

link.name: Microsoft: Fix distorted or crackling audio
link.description: Official guidance for testing audio enhancements, formats and driver-related sound problems.

checkAudioServices.title: Check Windows audio services
body: Press Windows + R, type services.msc and press Enter.
Find Windows Audio and Windows Audio Endpoint Builder.
Check that both services are running.
If either service has stopped or is experiencing problems, restart it.
Take care when changing services on a managed business computer.

link.name: Microsoft: Fix sound and audio problems
link.description: Includes instructions for checking and restarting Windows audio services.

restartAudioServices.title: Restart Windows audio services
body: In the Services console, restart Windows Audio and Windows Audio Endpoint Builder as appropriate.
Wait for the services to start and retest sound.
If a service cannot start, record the displayed error.
If sound is still missing, continue with the audio driver checks.

checkAudioDeviceManager.title: Check audio devices in Device Manager
body: Right-click Start and open Device Manager.
Expand Sound, video and game controllers.
Also check Audio inputs and outputs if present.
Look for missing devices, warning symbols or devices that have been disabled.
If no audio device is listed, try View, Show hidden devices and Action, Scan for hardware changes.
A missing or disabled audio device may indicate a driver or hardware problem.

link.name: Microsoft: Missing audio output device
link.description: Official instructions for diagnosing undetected audio devices and missing drivers.

checkAudioDeviceManager.alt: Windows Device Manager showing the Sound, video and game controllers category
checkAudioDeviceManager.caption: Expand Sound, video and game controllers to inspect installed audio devices.

updateAudioDriver.title: Update or reinstall the audio driver
body: In Device Manager, right-click the affected audio device and select Update driver.
Check the computer or motherboard manufacturer's support website for a compatible audio driver.
If necessary, uninstall the affected audio device and restart Windows to reinstall it.
Use the correct driver for the computer model and Windows version.
Retest sound after installation.

link.name: Microsoft: Audio driver troubleshooting
link.description: Official instructions for updating, reinstalling and diagnosing Windows audio drivers.

testAlternateAudioDevice.title: Test another audio device
body: Try a different known-working headset, pair of speakers or USB audio device.
Select the new device in Windows Sound settings.
Play a known working audio file or video.
If the replacement works, investigate the original audio device or its connection.
If no audio device works, continue investigating Windows or the computer hardware.

audioDeviceFault.title: Original audio device or connection fault likely
body: Sound works through an alternative audio device.
The original speakers, headset, audio port or connection may be faulty.
Check the original device on another computer if practical.
Repair or replace the affected hardware if necessary.

checkSystemUpdates.title: Check recent Windows or driver updates
body: Consider whether the sound stopped working immediately after a Windows or audio driver update.
Open Windows Update and review update history.
Check whether the audio driver was recently replaced.
If the timing matches a driver update, a driver rollback may restore sound.
If no update appears related, continue with further diagnostics.

link.name: Microsoft: Audio stopped after Windows Update
link.description: Official instructions for fixing sound problems following Windows or driver updates.

rollbackDriver.title: Roll back the audio driver
body: Open Device Manager and find the affected audio device.
Open Properties, select the Driver tab and choose Roll Back Driver if available.
Follow the prompts and restart the computer if requested.
Retest sound after the rollback.
If Roll Back Driver is unavailable, check the manufacturer's website for a previous compatible driver.

link.name: Microsoft: Repair audio after an update
link.description: Official instructions for rolling back the audio driver after a Windows update.

hardwareEscalation.title: Further audio diagnostics required
body: Audio is still not working after checking Windows settings, output devices, services and drivers.
The problem may involve the internal sound hardware, audio ports, motherboard or operating system.
Record the computer model, audio device and any Device Manager error codes.
Consider testing a USB audio adapter to help isolate a possible onboard audio fault.
Escalate for further software or hardware diagnosis.
